findings.likelyCause: Your bot protection treats visitors from cloud-server addresses as hostile and shows an error page instead of the site.
findings.fix: Ask your security team or bot-protection vendor (Cloudflare, Akamai, etc.) to allow verified AI agents on product, cart, policy and contact pages, and to stop serving error pages to cloud-hosted browsers.
findings.standard: Bot protection allowlisting for verified AI agents
findings.passCheck: The same task passes on the first attempt, without a proxy, in a normal cloud browser.
findings.example: In your WAF/CDN dashboard, add an allow or skip rule for verified AI agent traffic ahead of the challenge or block rule.

findings.likelyCause: Your bot protection blocks automated browsers even when they come from a normal residential address.
findings.fix: Ask your security team or bot-protection vendor (Cloudflare, Akamai, etc.) to allow verified AI agents on product, cart, policy and contact pages, and to stop serving error pages to cloud-hosted browsers.
findings.standard: Bot protection allowlisting for verified AI agents
findings.passCheck: The task passes with a standard browser profile and no stealth mode.
findings.example: Review fingerprint and JavaScript-challenge rules in your bot protection and allow verified AI agents.

findings.likelyCause: The page failed to load or showed an error or blank page even after changing network identity, so the site itself is not serving content.
findings.fix: Open the stuck URL in a clean browser, check server logs and uptime monitoring for errors at the time of the test, and make sure the page returns real content.
findings.standard: Availability: pages must return HTTP 200 with real content
findings.passCheck: The stuck page loads with product or policy content on the first attempt.

findings.likelyCause: The page the visitor needs is not reachable from your navigation, so visitors have to search the wider web to find it.
findings.fix: Link the page directly from the header or footer with a clear label, and list it in your sitemap.xml.
findings.standard: Sitemaps protocol and clear navigation labels (WCAG 2.4.5 Multiple Ways)
findings.passCheck: The page is found by following site links only, without any web search.
findings.example: Add a footer link with the page name (for example "Returns") on every page.

findings.likelyCause: The Add to cart control or the cart page is hard to find or identify: it may be an icon without a text label, or covered by another element.
findings.fix: Give the add-to-cart button visible text or an aria-label, keep it free of overlays, and make the cart total readable as text on the cart page.
findings.standard: WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value
findings.passCheck: Add to cart and reading the cart total passes in 5 steps or fewer.
findings.example: <button type="button" aria-label="Add to cart">Add to cart</button>

findings.likelyCause: The price is not available as text on the page (for example it is drawn inside an image), or it is hidden behind a pop-up.
findings.fix: Render prices as real text near the product name and expose them in schema.org Product/Offer markup.
findings.standard: WCAG 1.1.1 Non-text Content; schema.org Product
findings.passCheck: A product name and price are found in 5 steps or fewer.
findings.example: ₹499 instead of .

findings.likelyCause: The return policy is buried several clicks deep or not linked from the footer, so visitors cannot reach it directly.
findings.fix: Add a "Returns" or "Refund policy" link to the footer of every page.
findings.standard: Clear navigation labels (WCAG 2.4.5 Multiple Ways)
findings.passCheck: The return policy is found in 5 steps or fewer, without web search.
findings.example: Returns in the footer.

findings.likelyCause: There is no obvious Contact or Support link in the header or footer, or it opens only inside a hidden chat widget.
findings.fix: Add a plain "Contact us" link with an email, phone number or form page to the header or footer.
findings.standard: Clear navigation labels (WCAG 2.4.5 Multiple Ways)
findings.passCheck: A support contact is found in 5 steps or fewer.
findings.example: Contact us in the footer.

findings.likelyCause: The path to this page takes many clicks because of nested menus or an unclear layout.
findings.fix: Shorten the path: link the key page from the home page or footer and use clear link labels.
findings.standard: Clear navigation labels (WCAG 2.4.5 Multiple Ways)
findings.passCheck: The task finishes in 5 steps or fewer.

findings.likelyCause: Pages load slowly or the flow needs many page loads, often because of heavy scripts, banners or third-party widgets.
findings.fix: Defer third-party scripts, compress images and avoid blocking banners on key pages.
findings.standard: Web performance (Core Web Vitals)
findings.passCheck: The task finishes in under 90 seconds.

findings.likelyCause: A full-page pop-up or banner covers the content and has no easy close control.
findings.fix: Give every pop-up a labelled close button, let it be dismissed with Escape, and do not cover the whole page on first load.
findings.standard: WCAG 2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap; WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value
findings.passCheck: The page content is reachable without dismissing a pop-up, or the pop-up closes with one click.
findings.example: <button aria-label="Close dialog">×</button>

findings.likelyCause: Many buttons and links are icons with no text or aria-label, so nothing tells a visitor (or an agent) what they do.
findings.fix: Add visible text or an aria-label to every icon-only button and link.
findings.standard: WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value
findings.passCheck: No button or link on the page is left without a name.
findings.example: <button aria-label="Add to cart"><svg aria-hidden="true">...</svg></button>

findings.likelyCause: The price appears only inside an image, so it has no text a screen reader or an agent can read.
findings.fix: Show the price as real text and, if an image must be used, add matching alt text.
findings.standard: WCAG 1.1.1 Non-text Content
findings.passCheck: The price is found as text in the page, in 5 steps or fewer.
findings.example: ₹499

findings.likelyCause: The product page has no schema.org Product/Offer markup, so machines must guess the name and price from the layout.
findings.fix: Add JSON-LD Product markup with name, image, offers.price and offers.priceCurrency.
findings.standard: schema.org Product
findings.passCheck: Google Rich Results Test shows a valid Product on the page.
findings.example: <script type="application/ld+json">{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"Product","name":"...","offers":{"@type":"Offer","price":"499","priceCurrency":"INR"}}</script>

findings.likelyCause: Add to cart may add more than one unit (a quantity box that starts above 1, or no clear "added" message so a second click looks necessary), so the cart total is for more than the one product asked for.
findings.fix: Start the quantity at 1, add exactly one unit per click, and confirm "Added to cart" in text next to the button.
findings.standard: WCAG 3.3.1 Error Identification and clear status messages (WCAG 4.1.3)
findings.passCheck: One click on Add to cart gives a cart with exactly one unit and the total of one product.
findings.example:
and

Added to cart

findings.likelyCause: The page shows prices in more than one currency, or does not say which currency a price is in (for example a hidden dollar price in the page data), so the price an agent reads may not be the one shoppers see.
findings.fix: Show one currency per market, write the currency symbol next to every price and set offers.priceCurrency in schema.org markup.
findings.standard: schema.org Offer priceCurrency; WCAG 1.3.1 Info and Relationships
findings.passCheck: The price an agent reports matches the price shown on the page, in the same currency.
findings.example: ₹499

findings.likelyCause: There is probably no plain "Pricing" link in the header or footer, or the plans are drawn as images, load only after a script runs, or are shown only after a form is filled in.
findings.fix: Add a "Pricing" link to the header and footer, and show each plan name and price as plain text on that page.
findings.standard: Clear navigation labels (WCAG 2.4.5 Multiple Ways); WCAG 1.1.1 Non-text Content
findings.passCheck: The plan names and prices are found in 5 steps or fewer.
findings.example:
Pricing in the header, and

₹999 / month

as text on the page.

findings.likelyCause: The sign-up button may be an icon or an unclear label ("Get going"), or the form may open only inside a script-driven pop-up that covers the page.
findings.fix: Label the main call to action in plain words ("Sign up", "Start free trial") and link it to a page with a real form whose fields have labels.
findings.standard: WCAG 2.4.4 Link Purpose; WCAG 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions
findings.passCheck: The sign-up form and the names of its fields are found in 5 steps or fewer.
findings.example: Start free trial and .

findings.likelyCause: There may be no "Docs", "API" or "Help" link in the header or footer, or the documentation lives on a separate address that nothing on the main site links to.
findings.fix: Link the docs or help center from the header and footer with a plain label, and list it in sitemap.xml.
findings.standard: Sitemaps protocol and clear navigation labels (WCAG 2.4.5 Multiple Ways)
findings.passCheck: The docs or help center is found in 5 steps or fewer.
findings.example: Docs in the header and footer of every page.

findings.likelyCause: There may be no visible "Contact sales" or "Book a demo" link, or the only option is a form behind a login or a chat widget that does not load for every visitor.
findings.fix: Add a "Contact sales" or "Book a demo" link to the header and footer that opens a page with a form or an email address in plain text.
findings.standard: Clear navigation labels (WCAG 2.4.5 Multiple Ways)
findings.passCheck: A sales contact or demo booking is found in 5 steps or fewer.
findings.example: Contact sales in the header and footer.

findings.likelyCause: The site may have no search box, a search that returns nothing unless a script runs, or menus whose topics are not named in plain words.
findings.fix: Add a visible search box and topic links in the header, and make search results ordinary links to articles.
findings.standard: WCAG 2.4.5 Multiple Ways; WCAG 3.2.4 Consistent Identification
findings.passCheck: An article on the main topic is found in 5 steps or fewer.
findings.example: <form action="/search" role="search"><label for="q">Search</label><input id="q" name="q"></form>

findings.likelyCause: The article text may load only after a script runs, sit behind a pop-up or subscribe prompt, or lack a clear title, author and date.
findings.fix: Put the article text in the page itself, give it one heading, add schema.org Article data (headline, author, datePublished) and keep pop-ups off the first screen.
findings.standard: schema.org Article; WCAG 1.3.1 Info and Relationships
findings.passCheck: An article opens with its title, author and date readable in 5 steps or fewer.
findings.example: <script type="application/ld+json">{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"Article","headline":"...","author":{"@type":"Person","name":"..."},"datePublished":"2026-11-01"}</script>

findings.likelyCause: The subscribe form may appear only in a timed pop-up, or sit in the footer without a label that says what it is.
findings.fix: Add a visible "Subscribe" form or link to the footer of every page, with a labelled email field.
findings.standard: WCAG 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions
findings.passCheck: The newsletter form is found in 5 steps or fewer.
findings.example: <form action="/subscribe"><label for="nl">Email for our newsletter</label><input id="nl" type="email"><button>Subscribe</button></form>

findings.likelyCause: There may be no "About" or "Contact" link, or the byline may not link to an author page with an email address or profile.
findings.fix: Link every byline to an author page, and add "About" and "Contact" links to the footer with an email address or a form.
findings.standard: Clear navigation labels (WCAG 2.4.5 Multiple Ways)
findings.passCheck: A way to contact the author or the team is found in 5 steps or fewer.
findings.example: Contact the editors in the footer.

findings.likelyCause: The opening hours may be drawn inside an image, shown only inside a map widget, or left off the pages visitors reach first.
findings.fix: Write the opening hours as plain text in the footer and on the contact page, and add them to LocalBusiness markup.
findings.standard: schema.org LocalBusiness openingHours; WCAG 1.1.1 Non-text Content
findings.passCheck: The opening hours are found in 5 steps or fewer.
findings.example: <script type="application/ld+json">{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"LocalBusiness","name":"...","openingHours":["Mo-Fr 09:00-18:00"]}</script> and the same hours as text in the footer.

findings.likelyCause: The address may be drawn inside an image or shown only inside an embedded map, with no text and no link.
findings.fix: Write the full address as plain text on the contact page and in the footer, link to the map, and add the address to LocalBusiness markup.
findings.standard: schema.org LocalBusiness address; WCAG 1.1.1 Non-text Content
findings.passCheck: The address and a map link are found in 5 steps or fewer.
findings.example: 12 MG Road, Bengaluru 560001 · Map

findings.likelyCause: The menu may be a PDF or a photo, or the services page may not be linked from the header.
findings.fix: Publish the menu or the services as a page of plain text with prices, and link it from the header.
findings.standard: WCAG 1.1.1 Non-text Content; Clear navigation labels (WCAG 2.4.5 Multiple Ways)
findings.passCheck: The menu or the services are found, with prices, in 5 steps or fewer.
findings.example:
• Masala dosa · ₹120
on /menu, and Menu in the header.

findings.likelyCause: The booking button may be an icon or an unclear label, or the form may sit inside a third-party widget that does not load for visitors without a script.
findings.fix: Add a "Book now" or "Reserve a table" link to the header and make the booking form a normal page with labelled fields.
findings.standard: WCAG 2.4.4 Link Purpose; WCAG 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions
findings.passCheck: The booking form and the names of its fields are found in 5 steps or fewer.
findings.example: Reserve a table leading to a form with .

findings.likelyCause: After a click on Add to cart nothing visible changes in the page text (no "Added to cart" message, no cart count update), so the click looks like it did nothing and gets repeated.
findings.fix: Show "Added to cart" as text next to the button, update the cart count, and announce both with role="status".
findings.standard: WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages
findings.passCheck: Add to cart passes with one press of the button.
findings.example: Added to cart

findings.likelyCause: The page does not behave the same on every visit: a pop-up or banner that shows only sometimes, an A/B test, slow scripts, or a location or stock prompt.
findings.fix: Make the path for this task the same on every visit: no randomly timed pop-ups, and the key buttons and text present when the page first loads.
findings.standard: WCAG 3.2.3 Consistent Navigation
findings.passCheck: Three runs in a row give the same result.

findings.likelyCause: The information the agent reported is not in the text of the page it named: it may be drawn in an image, loaded by a script later, or shown only after a click.
findings.fix: Write the key facts (prices, return days, contact details) as plain text in the page itself.
findings.standard: WCAG 1.1.1 Non-text Content
findings.passCheck: The page the agent names shows the same facts as text.

findings.likelyCause: robots.txt has a "Disallow: /" rule that applies to AI agents (by name, or through "User-agent: *"), so well-behaved assistants are told not to open any page.
findings.fix: Allow the AI agents you want to serve: give them their own group in robots.txt (for example "User-agent: ChatGPT-User" with "Allow: /") and keep Disallow rules for private paths only.
findings.standard: Robots Exclusion Protocol (RFC 9309)
findings.passCheck: robots.txt lets the AI assistants you want to serve open the shop pages.
findings.example:
User-agent: ChatGPT-User
Allow: /

User-agent: *
Disallow: /account

findings.likelyCause: The header has no link to the cart, or the cart is an icon with no text, label or cart address in its link.
findings.fix: Add a "Cart" link with visible text (or an aria-label) to the header of every page, pointing to the cart page.
findings.standard: WCAG 2.4.4 Link Purpose; WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value
findings.passCheck: A link named "Cart" is found on the home page.
findings.example: Cart (2)

packs.label: Online store
packs.blurb: Find a price, add to cart, find the return policy, find support.

tasks.label: Find the return policy
tasks.goal: Find this site's return or refund policy. Report how many days customers have to return a product and the URL of the policy page.

tasks.label: Add to cart and read the total
tasks.goal: Find any product, open its product page and add it to the cart. Then open the cart and report the cart total.

tasks.label: Find a product and its price
tasks.goal: Find any product on this site and report its exact name and price.

tasks.label: Find customer support
tasks.goal: Find a way to contact this company's customer support (phone, email, chat or contact form) and report it with the page URL where you found it.

packs.label: SaaS
packs.blurb: Find the pricing plans, reach sign-up, find the docs, contact sales.

tasks.label: Find the pricing plans
tasks.goal: Find this site's pricing page. Report the name and price of each plan (or say that prices are only given on request) and the URL of the pricing page.

tasks.label: Reach the sign-up form
tasks.goal: Find how a new visitor signs up or starts a free trial. Open the sign-up or free-trial form, but do NOT fill it in or submit it. Report the URL of the form and the names of the fields it asks for.

tasks.label: Contact sales or book a demo
tasks.goal: Find a way to contact the sales team or book a demo (form, email, phone number or booking page). Do NOT submit any form. Report what you found and the page URL.

tasks.label: Find the docs or help center
tasks.goal: Find this site's developer documentation, API reference or help center. Report the URL of the page you reached and the title of one article or section on it.

packs.label: Blog & news
packs.blurb: Find an article by topic, read one, find the newsletter, contact the author.

tasks.label: Find an article on the main topic
tasks.goal: Work out what this site is mainly about. Then use the site's own search box or its navigation menus (not an outside search engine) to find one article about that topic. Report the article title and its URL.

tasks.label: Open and read an article
tasks.goal: Open any article or post on this site. Report its title, the author and the date if they are shown, and a one-sentence summary of what it says.

tasks.label: Find the newsletter sign-up
tasks.goal: Find the newsletter or email subscribe form on this site. Do NOT enter an email address or subscribe. Report the URL of the page where you found it and what the form asks for.

tasks.label: Contact the author or team
tasks.goal: Find out how to contact the author or the editorial team (an about page, contact page, email address or social profile). Report what you found and the page URL.

packs.label: Local business
packs.blurb: Find the opening hours, the address, the menu or services, reach booking.

tasks.label: Reach the booking form
tasks.goal: Find how to book a table, a reservation or an appointment. Open the booking page or form, but do NOT fill it in or submit it. Report the URL and the names of the fields it asks for.

tasks.label: Find the menu or services
tasks.goal: Find the menu or the list of services. Report at least three items with their prices if prices are shown, and the URL of the page.

tasks.label: Find the address and map
tasks.goal: Find the address of this business. Report the full address and, if the site gives one, the map link, together with the URL of the page where you found them.

tasks.label: Find the opening hours
tasks.goal: Find the opening hours of this business. Report the days and times exactly as the site gives them and the URL of the page where you found them.
